He was telling me at Thanksgiving about the stress testing they have to do for suspension cables, and it's fascinating how much tension those things can hold. They use these massive hydraulic rigs to pull the cables until they snap, just to see what the breaking point is. I can't even imagine the sound that makes when it finally gives way... \n\nAnyway, what was the question? Less sleep? No, I need my sleep. I'm pretty regular with it, honestly.\n\nDoctor: Do you think these people are using technology, like cameras, microphones, or computer systems, to monitor you?\n\nPatient: Cameras or microphones? I... I haven't found any bugs or anything like that. But I came in because for a while now, I’ve been convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. They don't necessarily need microphones, they do it by sending me little signals. It's in the invitations I get, or the panel topics they choose, or even exactly who sits near me at these networking events. \n\nLike, they always have these assigned seating charts at the big galas. I went to this one at the art museum last month, and they had this incredible exhibit of local 19th-century pottery set up in the main hall. Rookwood pottery, I think it's called. The glazing on those pieces is just beautiful. They use this technique where the colors kind of bleed into each other before they fire it in the kiln. My grandmother had a vase just like that on her fireplace mantle. She was absolutely terrified of anyone breaking it, so we were never allowed to play in the front room. We had to stay in the den, which had this awful orange shag carpet. It was the 70s, so I guess that was the style, but man, it was ugly. It held onto dog hair like crazy, too. We had a golden retriever named Buster who shed constantly, and my mom was always dragging out this massive Hoover vacuum just to keep the floor clean...\n\nSorry, I lost my train of thought. Oh, the tracking. Right. Yeah, so they send these signals with the invitations and who they seat me next to. And even when I try to tell myself it could just be a coincidence, I just can’t really let it go. It happens too much to just be random.\n\nDoctor: Have other people told you that your emotions or facial expressions seem flat or limited?\n\nPatient: Flat? I don't know if anyone's said \"flat,\" exactly. But they definitely notice something's off. I mean, I still get my work done, mostly. Just in pieces. But I don't really have that same spark I used to. I’ll just leave client follow-ups sitting on my desk for days. \n\nI actually have this antique brass letter opener I use for my mail. I bought it at this flea market down by the river. It's shaped like a little sword, with all this intricate engraving on the hilt. The guy who sold it to me said it was from the Civil War era, but who knows if that's true. Those flea market vendors will tell you anything to make a sale. I used to go down there every Sunday morning with my buddy Dave. We'd grab coffee and just wander around looking at all the junk. Dave is really into restoring old pocket watches. He has this whole setup in his basement with these tiny screwdrivers and magnifying glasses. It's crazy how many little gears and springs are inside those things. I don't have the patience for it, honestly. My hands shake too much when I try to do anything that precise. I tried to build a model airplane once when I was a kid, one of those balsa wood ones, and I just ended up gluing my fingers together...\n\nWhat was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, I just don't have the energy for things anymore. I skip my jazz nights, I don't go to pickup basketball. And I don't really care that I'm missing it, honestly. When friends ask what's going on, I just give them really short answers. Talking just feels like so much effort lately. Too much effort.\n\nDoctor: Have you felt suspicious or distrustful of other people for as long as you can remember, or is this a newer change?\n\nPatient: For as long as I can remember? No, no, it's definitely a newer change. I mean, these changes have been building since that arts nonprofit recognition a little over two years ago. They gave me this big glass award at the dinner for helping them restructure their endowment. It was this really thick, etched glass thing. I actually dropped it on my way to the parking garage that night and chipped the bottom corner, which was super annoying. \n\nIt reminded me of this time I went to a glass-blowing workshop up in Toledo. Have you ever seen them do that? They take this glowing, molten blob out of a furnace that's like two thousand degrees, and they just spin it on this long metal tube. It's completely mesmerizing. The guy teaching the class made this intricate little glass swan in about three minutes flat. I tried to make a simple paperweight and it ended up looking like a squashed tomato. We had to leave it in this special cooling oven overnight so it wouldn't shatter from the temperature drop. I ended up giving it to my mom for Mother's Day anyway, and she still keeps it on her kitchen windowsill. She has all these African violets lined up there. You have to water them from the bottom, apparently, or the leaves rot. She has this special copper watering can with a really long, thin spout just for that. It gets tarnished pretty fast, though, so she's always polishing it...\n\nWait, what did you ask me? About the timeline? Yeah, it hasn't been my whole life. My vision is actually pretty sharp, though I do wear these blue-light blocking glasses when I'm staring at client portfolios all day. I bought them online from this startup company that supposedly plants a tree for every pair you buy. It's a neat concept, honestly. I think they plant them somewhere in the Pacific Northwest, like Oregon or Washington. \n\nI went to Seattle a few years ago for a wealth management seminar and it rained the entire time I was there. I didn't even bring an umbrella, so I had to buy one from this little tourist shop near Pike Place Market. Have you ever been there? They actually throw the fish right over the counter when you order. It's wild to watch. I bought some smoked salmon to take home, but they packed it in this dry ice that started smoking in my rental car on the way to the airport. I got so worried the rental company was going to charge me a massive cleaning fee because the whole trunk smelled like a campfire. The guy at the return desk didn't even blink, though. He just scanned the barcode on the windshield and told me to have a good flight... \n\nWait, sorry, what did you ask me? About seeing things? Right. No, no, I don't see things that aren't there. Just the tracking stuff I mentioned before.\n\nDoctor: When you think about the possibility that these signals are just coincidences, how certain are you that the tracking is really happening?\n\nPatient: How certain? I'm convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. They send me these little signals, you know? Through the invitations I get, the specific panel topics they choose, or even who they seat near me at these events. \n\nLike last month, there was this panel at the Duke Energy Convention Center downtown. The cheese was so thick you had to eat it with a knife and fork, which completely defeats the purpose of pizza if you ask me. Yeah. Even when I try to brush the signals off and tell myself it's just random chance, I can't. No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't really watch much live TV anyway, mostly just streaming stuff. I did watch this documentary the other night about the history of the postal service, though. It was actually fascinating. They talked about how the Pony Express only lasted for like 18 months before the telegraph made it obsolete. Can you imagine riding a horse across the country at full speed just to deliver some mail? \n\nThey showed this one guy who rode for them, and he had to carry this special leather pouch called a mochila that fit right over the saddle. He told me I needed to condition it every six months with this specific beeswax polish or it would dry out and crack. I bought a tin of the polish from him, but it's completely rock hard now. I think you're supposed to heat it up with a hair dryer before you use it, but I always forget. I tried using a lighter on it once and almost set the whole tin on fire. My smoke alarm went off and my dog started howling... \n\nWait, what was the question? Oh, about the TV and newspapers being about me? No, nothing like that. Just the things with the client meetings I mentioned.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any periods when your mood was unusually high, excited, or irritable at the same time these beliefs were happening?\n\nPatient: High or excited? No, I wouldn't say that. My mood's been pretty level. I mean, I get stressed sometimes, sure, but not like, unusually hyped up or irritable. I try to keep things pretty even-keeled. I actually started drinking this chamomile tea at night to help me wind down. It's supposed to be really good for relaxation. I buy it loose-leaf from this little spice shop over in the Over-the-Rhine neighborhood. \n\nThey have these huge glass jars lining the walls, filled with every kind of tea and spice you can imagine. The guy who runs it is always wearing this faded denim apron with flour all over it, even though I'm pretty sure he doesn't bake anything there. I think I overwatered them. Or maybe it was the soil. I bought this cheap potting mix from the hardware store that had these weird little white foam balls in it. I read somewhere that those are supposed to help with drainage, but I don't know, it just looked like shredded Styrofoam cups to me. \n\nSpeaking of Styrofoam, did you know some cities are completely banning it for takeout containers? My uncle had to cut down three massive ash trees in his backyard because of those bugs. He rented this heavy-duty wood chipper to mulch them all up, and it was so loud you could hear it from three streets over. He ended up with a mountain of mulch, and he completely ruined his grass trying to spread it all out with a wheelbarrow. Those wheelbarrows with the single tire in the front are so hard to balance if you overfill them. You hit one rock and the whole thing tips over into the mud... \n\nWait, I'm sorry.
